title: Microsoft Purview: Microsoft Graph APIs for archive mailboxes as EWS retires (GCC, GCC High and DoD)
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, EWS controls, licensing statements and archive API behaviour are supported. It correctly distinguishes GCC's worldwide Graph endpoint from GCC High and DoD, and does not treat that mapping as proof of archive API rollout.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans Graph access to main and auxiliary archive mailboxes.
claims.quote: Access to Archive mailboxes (Main + Auxiliary) through Microsoft Graph.

claims.claim: The roadmap's goal is a single archive view despite data residing across auxiliary mailboxes.
claims.quote: The goal is to give users a single, seamless Archive view, even though Archive data may physically reside across multiple auxiliary mailboxes

claims.claim: Auto-expanding archiving creates auxiliary archive mailboxes.
claims.quote: An archive mailbox can include a main archive mailbox and one or more auxiliary archive mailboxes (created through autoexpanding archive).

claims.claim: A folder can appear in the main archive while its contents reside in an auxiliary archive.
claims.quote: In some cases, a folder appears in the main archive mailbox, but its contents actually reside in an auxiliary archive mailbox.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Accessing a folder in an auxiliary archive can return HTTP 308 Permanent Redirect.
claims.quote: When you access a folder that physically resides in an auxiliary archive mailbox, the API returns an HTTP 308 Permanent Redirect with a Location header.

claims.claim: The application follows the folder redirect by requesting the URL in the response.
claims.quote: Make a new request using the URL from the Location header.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: An export response can contain ErrorArchiveFolderMovedPermanently for items in an auxiliary archive.
claims.quote: some items in the response might include an ErrorArchiveFolderMovedPermanently error instead of data. This indicates that the item physically resides in an auxiliary archive mailbox.

claims.claim: The application retries an affected export against the URL supplied in the error.
claims.quote: For the item that returned ErrorArchiveFolderMovedPermanently, make a new POST request to the URL in the error message with the item ID to export it.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Importing to a folder physically located in an auxiliary archive can return HTTP 409 Conflict.
claims.quote: When you attempt to import an item into a folder that physically resides in an auxiliary (autoexpanded) archive mailbox, you receive an HTTP 409 Conflict response that indicates the correct target mailbox.

claims.claim: Resolving the import conflict requires a new import session targeting the mailbox named in the error.
claims.quote: create a new import session targeting the mailbox ID indicated in the error message

claims.claim: Well-known folder names are not supported for archive mailboxes.
claims.quote: Well-known folder names aren't supported for archive mailboxes.

claims.claim: Applications reference archive folders by folder ID.
claims.quote: Reference folders in archive mailboxes by folder ID rather than by well-known folder name.

claims.quote: | Sovereign Cloud availability | Make Exchange workload APIs required for EWS migration available in supported sovereign clouds. | Q4 CY2026 |

claims.claim: The EWS parity-gap dates are estimates that might change.
claims.quote: Estimated availability dates are targets and might change.

claims.claim: GCC uses the worldwide Microsoft Graph endpoint.
claims.quote: If you're working in a Microsoft 365 GCC environment, continue using the worldwide endpoints: https://portal.azure.com and https://graph.microsoft.com.

claims.claim: GCC High maps to Microsoft Graph US Government L4.
claims.quote: | Microsoft Graph for US Government L4 (GCC High) | https://graph.microsoft.us | Not supported. |

claims.claim: The endpoint mapping does not publish a GCC rollout date for archive mailbox access.
claims.quote: Searched: "archive" "Graph" "GCC" mailbox availability. Read graph/deployments, mailbox exportItems and List folders, and the EWS deprecation page; none gives a GCC-specific archive rollout date beyond the roadmap target.

claims.claim: Roadmap item 567313 describes the Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant) equivalent.

claims.claim: The Worldwide item's status is Rolling out.
claims.quote: 567313: "status": "Rolling out"

claims.quote: 567313: "targetDate": "October CY2026"

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Learn says EWS starts to be disabled globally for all organizations in October 2026.
claims.quote: October 2026: EWS starts to be disabled globally for all organizations.

claims.claim: Learn says EWS is fully disabled in April 2027.
claims.quote: April 2027: EWS is fully disabled.

claims.claim: Learn has no dedicated page for this roadmap item in GCC, GCC High and DoD.
claims.quote: Searched: "archive" "Graph" "573701"; "archive" "Graph" "GCC" mailbox availability. Read deployments, redirects, exportItems, List folders and EWS deprecation; found general API documentation, not an item-specific government-cloud page.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated what the Graph archive change does on arrival if administrators take no action.
claims.quote: Searched: "archive" "Graph" "default" mailbox APIs; Microsoft Graph archive mailbox APIs GCC GCC High DoD enable disable tenant setting default availability 573701. Read roadmap, redirects and import/export overview; no rollout default is stated.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No tenant setting specifically turning the Graph archive APIs on or off is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "archive" "Graph" "tenant" "enable" mailbox APIs; Microsoft Graph archive mailbox APIs GCC GCC High DoD enable disable tenant setting default availability 573701. Read redirects, import/export overview and API permissions; no API-specific tenant switch found.

claims.claim: Full-fidelity export provides mailbox item content.
claims.quote: Export Exchange mailboxItem objects in full fidelity. This API exports each item as an opaque stream.

claims.claim: The mailbox import and export APIs are not designed for mailbox backup and restore.
claims.quote: The mailbox import and export APIs in Microsoft Graph aren't designed for mailbox backup and restore.

claims.quote: Note: User Agent based blocking also impacts connections using REST/Graph API

claims.quote: Use the importUrl property from the new session response to retry the import.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No meter for the mailbox import and export APIs appears in Microsoft's published metered API list.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph mailbox import export API archive license pricing metered. Read graph/metered-api-list and graph/metered-api-overview; the list contains assignSensitivityLabel, not mailbox import or export.

claims.claim: Standard Graph APIs are available within defined usage thresholds as part of the user licence without additional costs.
claims.quote: Access to standard APIs within the defined usage thresholds is available as part of the user license without additional costs.

claims.claim: Graph's high-capacity category includes purpose-built bulk export or import endpoints.
claims.quote: This category includes purpose-built, bulk export or import endpoints and Microsoft Graph services.

claims.claim: High-capacity Graph APIs might be metered beyond user subscription licences.
claims.quote: These APIs might be metered and incur additional costs beyond user subscription licenses.

claims.claim: The published Graph metered API list contains one API, assignSensitivityLabel.
claims.quote: | SharePoint and OneDrive for Business assignSensitivityLabel | $0.00185 (USD) per API call

claims.claim: The published assignSensitivityLabel rate is $0.00185 USD per API call.
claims.quote: $0.00185 (USD) per API call

claims.claim: Metered Graph APIs are available only in the global environment, not national clouds, including GCC using the worldwide endpoint.
claims.quote: Metered APIs and services in Microsoft Graph are currently available only in the Microsoft global environment and not in national cloud deployments, including Microsoft 365 GCC deployments accessed through the worldwide Microsoft Graph endpoint.

claims.claim: The organisation-wide EWS control is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Show all > Settings > Org Settings > Security and Privacy > Baseline Security Mode > Authentication > Disable organization-wide access to Exchange Web Services (EWS).
claims.quote: select ... Show all ... Settings ... Org Settings ... Security and Privacy ... Baseline Security Mode ... Authentication ... Disable organization-wide access to Exchange Web Services (EWS)

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Set-OrganizationConfig -EwsEnabled $false blocks the organisation from using EWS.
claims.quote: | Block the entire organization from using EWS. | Set-OrganizationConfig -EwsEnabled:$false

claims.claim: Learn says the way EwsEnabled operates changes in October 2026.
claims.quote: The way the EWSEnabled parameter operates will change in October 2026 due to the EWS Deprecation.

claims.claim: Disabling EWS organisation-wide also disables per-user EWS overrides.
claims.quote: Disabling EWS in the organization also disables per-user EWS overrides.

claims.claim: The organisation-wide EWS setting controls EWS rather than the Graph archive APIs.
claims.quote: EWS is disabled for the user or organization. The applicable EwsEnabled setting prevents access. Organization-wide disablement also blocks users whose mailbox-level setting is enabled.

claims.claim: The EWS usage report is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Reports > Usage > Reports > Exchange > EWS usage.
claims.quote: In the navigation menu, select Reports. ... Select Usage. ... On the Usage page, under Reports, select Exchange. ... On the report page, select the EWS usage tab.

claims.claim: No API or PowerShell operation for the EWS usage report is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Exchange EWS usage report Graph API PowerShell getEwsUsage report; "EWS usage" "API" report; site:learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/reportroot "EWS". Read EWS usage and graph/api/resources/report; no operation for this report found.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The EWS usage report shows SOAP actions by application ID for applications calling EWS in the organisation.
claims.quote: The following table provides a breakdown of the EWS usage per SOAP action by each active application in your tenant during the selected period.

claims.claim: EWS usage data is collected and aggregated weekly.
claims.quote: Usage data is collected and aggregated weekly, not daily.

claims.claim: EWS usage can take up to 10 days to appear in the report.
claims.quote: It can take up to 10 days for usage to show in the report.

claims.claim: The EWS usage report is a read-only report, not a control over Graph archive access.
claims.quote: The Exchange Web Services (EWS) usage report displays the SOAP actions used by each application calling EWS in your organization. It also shows the successful-call volume for each SOAP action.

claims.claim: The EWS deprecation page links to EWS-to-Graph API mappings.
claims.quote: Many application scenarios are already supported with direct mappings between EWS operations and Graph APIs.

claims.claim: The EWS deprecation page links to the EWS Analyzer tool.
claims.quote: To simplify and accelerate your analysis and migration, we introduced the EWS Usage Reports, the EWS Analyzer tool, and a tutorial for AI assisted code analysis and refactoring.

claims.claim: The cited exportItems reference and its national-cloud table are available in the v1.0 reference.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/admin/exchange/mailboxes/MBX:e0643f21@a7809c93/exportItems

claims.claim: Microsoft's documentation does not publish the vendor upgrade fees that might accompany EWS migration.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph EWS migration vendor upgrade fees costs. Read EWS deprecation, migration overview search excerpt, Graph metering overview and metered API list; Microsoft advises coordinating with vendors but publishes no vendor upgrade fees.
